results.title: Text Embeddings Inference: Serve Embeddings for RAG on a GPU
results.author: Faiz Ahmed
highlights:
Faiz Ahmed Oct 1, 2026· 14 min read

...

RTX A6000, from $0.48/GPU-hr.

Text Embeddings Inference (TEI) is Hugging Face's server for embedding and reranker models, and the fastest way to run it is the Docker image built for your GPU's architecture. The current release is 1.9.4, from 2026-09-15. On QuantaCloud that means the Bare Metal template, one container published on 127.0.0.1 with an API key, and a RAG app that calls `/v1/embeddings` the way it would call OpenAI. QuantaCloud has no managed embedding endpoint, so this is self-hosted inference: the container and its security are yours to run.

...

TEI ships one image per GPU architecture, and the tag has to match the GPU's compute capability. These are the 1.9.4 tags for the GPUs QuantaCloud rents:

| GPU on QuantaCloud | Compute capability | Image |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A100 80GB, SXM4 and PCIe | 8.0 | `ghcr.io/huggingface/text-embeddings-inference:1.9.4` |
| RTX A6000 | 8.6 | `ghcr.io/huggingface/text-embeddings-inference:86-1.9.4` |
| L40S, L40, RTX 6000 Ada | 8.9 | `ghcr.io/huggingface/text-embeddings-inference:89-1.9.4` |
| H100 PCIe, H200 NVL | 9.0 | `ghcr.io/huggingface/text-embeddings-inference:hopper-1.9.4` |
| RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell | 12.0 | `ghcr.io/huggingface/text-embeddings-inference:120-1.9.4`, marked experimental |

...

## Throughput and cost per million tokens#

Throughput is what you pay for, because every model above fits every GPU. The cost of embedding a million tokens is the hourly price divided by (tokens per second x 3,600), times 1,000,000. Today's prices for the RTX A6000, L40S and H100 PCIe:

| GPU | Memory | From | Available now |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| RTX A6000 | 48 GB | $0.48/GPU-hr | Yes |
| L40S | 48 GB | $1.09/GPU-hr | Yes |
| H100 PCIe | 80 GB | $2.59/GPU-hr | Yes |

...

Stopping the instance terminates it and deletes its disk: the image, the model cache and anything stored next to them. Keep the vector database your app writes to off the VM, or copy it off before you stop, because there are no volumes or snapshots. The next launch pulls the 3.1 GB image and the model again, 2.27 GB for bge-m3, so keep the `docker run` line in a script, and see downloading Hugging Face models fast to shorten the wait. The first hour is charged at launch and the unused seconds are refunded when you stop (pricing).

...

### Which GPU should I rent for TEI?

The lowest-priced one that keeps up with your queue. On 2026-09-27 that was the RTX A6000, from $0.48/GPU-hr today, and the largest model above, Qwen3-Embedding-8B, needs about 15.1 GB of its 48 GB. Move to an L40S or an H100 PCIe when your own benchmark shows more tokens per dollar there.

results.title: Whisper on a GPU: faster-whisper, WhisperX and Diarization
results.author: Faiz Ahmed
highlights:
Faiz Ahmed Nov 12, 2026· 9 min read

The smallest GPU on offer is the right one, because Whisper is small and every GPU QuantaCloud rents has at least 48 GB. OpenAI publishes the memory each model needs in its own PyTorch implementation, and faster-whisper, which runs the same weights on the CTranslate2 inference engine, needs less.

| Model | Parameters | faster-whisper download |

...

Against the 46,068 MiB an RTX A6000 reports with ECC on, that batched run would fill about 13% of the card (our calculation: 6,090 / 46,068). The rest does nothing for a transcription job, which is why I choose the GPU on price. The RTX A6000 had the lowest price in the catalog on 2026-09-27, $0.48 an hour (today: $0.48/GPU-hr). A bigger card only pays off if it is faster by more than it costs: the H100 PCIe was $2.59 an hour that day (today: the console price), 5.4 times the A6000 (our calculation: 2.59 / 0.48), so it would have to transcribe more than 5.4 times as fast to cost less per hour of audio.

...

The last command is a dry run with checksums, and it lists no files when both sides match. Moving files to and from a GPU server covers object storage for large batches. For a queue that runs overnight, turn on auto top-up: if your balance cannot cover the next hour, QuantaCloud terminates the instance and deletes its disk, finished transcripts and all. The idle GPU guide stops the instance once the queue is done. You pay from launch to stop: the first hour is charged at launch and the unused seconds are refunded when you stop (pricing).

...

The number that decides the cost is speed, written as RTFx: seconds of audio transcribed per second of processing, the measure Hugging Face's Open ASR Leaderboard reports. The cost of an hour of audio is the hourly price divided by RTFx, so a GPU that is twice as fast and costs twice as much per hour gives the same cost per hour of audio.

You rent 48 GB on QuantaCloud because that is the smallest card on offer, and the RTX A6000 was the lowest-priced one on 2026-09-27. Speech in the other direction is no bigger: open-source text-to-speech models compares the open voice models, and none of them needs a 48 GB card either.
